commit_scope: Reuse one deep API health snapshot per public verification attempt so deployment proof cannot amplify serving-process load.

task_card.goal: Keep Hati Sheet tracking available while public deployment verification proves health, SHA parity, native authority, CORS, and pulse state.
done_when: One deep API health response is reused by direct health, SHA-parity, and fkwu-authority checks within each verifier attempt.
CORS availability uses the lightweight ping route and web health-proxy proof performs one request instead of two.
Focused verifier tests, local guards, exact-head CI/review, rollout, observer, public probes, and authenticated Hati Sheet recovery pass.
constraints: Preserve deployed-SHA, fkwu-authority, persistence, web-proxy, CORS, pulse, and public-page evidence.
Keep the private Sheet restricted and preserve the authenticated server-side read path.
Do not expose household tokens, balances, transaction rows, Sheet secrets, SSH material, or private URLs.

evidence_refs: Hostinger activation run 38074213429 deployed merge 86b6229459923788c5514919e4a53ff2fce42046 and initially marked the API container healthy.

The complete grounded sidecar finished, then three broad public verification attempts repeatedly read deep health and the API became slow, silent, and finally unreachable while the static Hati shell remained available.
A same-SHA recovery rerun restored lightweight ping before this repair was authored.
The focused regression proves SHA and fkwu checks reuse the captured health snapshot without another direct API health request.

Fresh exact-head review found that deduplicating the web health-proxy read had removed rollout-status patience; the focused regression now proves a transient 503 settles without restoring the duplicate request.

A second exact-head review found that concurrent gateway and SHA deadlines shortened the effective settling window; the regression now advances a fake clock through 89 seconds of gateway recovery and a stale SHA at 210 seconds, proving SHA patience starts after proxy recovery.

A third exact-head review found the reverse ordering: a stale SHA could outlive a gateway clock that had never seen an outage. Gateway patience now starts on the first transient response, and the regression proves stale-SHA-then-503 recovery independently.

A fourth exact-head review found gateway downtime still consumed the active SHA deadline. The verifier now extends SHA patience by the measured outage interval, and the regression proves stale SHA at t=0, outage from t=100 to t=189, stale SHA at recovery, and target SHA at t=260.

A fifth exact-head review found curl retry time before a transport failure was returned remained unmeasured. Proxy attempt timing now starts before the request, and the regression proves an 81-second request gap, stale recovery, a later stale check past the former deadline, and eventual target parity.
No household token, balance, transaction row, Sheet secret, SSH material, or private URL is present in this evidence.

local_validation.summary: Snapshot reuse, request-start outage accounting, healthy-time SHA patience, first-failure gateway patience in both rollout orderings, pulse, CSS, Hostinger path, shell syntax, and whitespace proofs pass. Evidence validation and full local guards are part of the pre-commit gate.
